plan: My goal is to maximize profit. In a second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy, meaning it's always the best strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because bidding below my value risks losing a profitable auction, and bidding above my value risks winning an auction at a price higher than my value. Since the value is drawn independently each round, past rounds don't directly influence the optimal strategy for this round, which is to bid my true value.

My goal is to maximize long-term profit. Since this is the first round and I have no history to learn from, I will bid my true value. This strategy is optimal in a second-price auction as it guarantees a non-negative profit if I win and maximizes my chances of winning when it's profitable.

My goal is to maximize long-term profit. Given this is a single round, I need to maximize profit for this round. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, my optimal strategy is to bid my true value. This ensures I only win if my value is higher than the second-highest bid, guaranteeing a non-negative profit. Bidding below my value risks losing a profitable opportunity. Bidding above my value risks winning and paying more than my value if the second-highest bid is between my value and my inflated bid.
